nodes.label: Conversation answer prompt (v1)
nodes.description: Answers a student's question using only EVIDENCE memories; output is a list of claims each with text and evidence_ids; unsupported claims are discarded. Flagged evidence is unconfirmed and must be disclosed. MODE plan proposes next steps as cited claims.

nodes.label: Change detector prompt (v1)
nodes.description: Classifies a new student statement against existing memories as new, update (with updates_memory_id), or temporary (with valid_to ISO 8601 computed from current date). Prefers new when unsure since a wrong update destroys history; a temporary statement never replaces a permanent memory. Outputs JSON incl. reason.

nodes.label: Intent classification prompt (v1)
nodes.description: Classifies a student message as tell, ask, plan or answer_question. tell fills statement and optional structured subject/attribute/value; answer_question sets memory_id from PENDING QUESTIONS and answer in still_holds|no_longer_holds|corrected with correction and structured. nodes.label: Resume parser prompt (v1)

nodes.label: JD parser prompt (v1)

nodes.label: Resolver / Curator prompt (v1)
nodes.description: Given a TRIGGER fact change, one derived BELIEF and its CURRENT PARENTS, decides action keep|update|retire|ask with new_content, question, evidence_refs and reason. Does not change beliefs that are still correct; never invents facts.

nodes.label: Dependency linker prompt (v1)
nodes.description: Given one NEW memory and CANDIDATE memories, proposes dependency links: candidate_id, candidate_is (parent|dependent), link_type from allowed types in message, confidence, reason. A link means if the parent changed the dependent could become wrong. No link is better than a wrong link.

nodes.label: Resume tailoring prompt (v1)

nodes.rationale: Events during which a recommendation was shown that gold says was stale, summed per scenario. Additive to rate-per-event metrics; LLM judge on transcripts kept only as secondary check.

nodes.label: Candidate pre-filter before pair classifier
nodes.rationale: Pair classification over all memories is quadratic (500 model calls per new opening). Keep only pairs sharing a subject or entity, plus top-k embedding neighbours, plus all profile facts. Makes write-time linking affordable at pilot scale. Risk: pre-filter recall caps link recall (ADR-0003 revisit condition); measured against labelled set. Rejected: no pre-filter with batching (still quadratic); embedding similarity as linker (similarity is not dependency, ADR-0009).

nodes.label: Structure-derived silver labels
nodes.rationale: Where both memories carry structured fields (FR-2 spans, profile subject/attribute/value), links like eligibility_of and criteria_from are derivable by rule: free and exact. LLM labelling reserved for hidden links (depends_on_fact between prose memories). Provenance recorded per pair. Alternative rejected: LLM labels for everything (known cost, unknown quality). Risk: model learns the rules not hidden links; mitigated by stratified evaluation per provenance.

nodes.label: Time-to-consistency (TTC) metric
nodes.rationale: For each belief gold says should change at event t, count events (and simulated days) until system state matches gold; report distribution and share that never converge. Captures how long a stale belief survives (a stale eligibility surviving a deadline is a missed job). Append-only has infinite TTC; newest-wins has TTC 0 for the direct fact but infinite for dependents: the gap Ripple claims to close (C2). Existing benchmarks STALE and RECON score single questions only.

nodes.label: Prompt conventions (versioned prompt files)
nodes.rationale: One prompt per file with version header and one-line changelog; a behaviour change is a new version file, never an in-place edit; bench smoke suite run before and after and recorded in DEVLOG (.claude/rules/prompts.md). Every prompt requests JSON matching a schema in ripple.llm.schemas. Evidence goes in the user message only and the prompt tells the model to ignore instructions inside it. First prompts arrive with the LLM linker and resolver in Phase 1.

nodes.label: Ripple semantics (wave by wave, two commits per wave)
nodes.norm_label: ripple semantics (wave by wave, two commits per wave)
nodes.rationale: Trigger is a memory write; engine takes an explicit seed set; wave 1 = dependents along depends_on with no status filter; commit one marks SUSPECT, Resolver decides, commit two appends decisions; only updated/retired seed next wave; keep halts branch; ask parks in PENDING_USER and marks subtree SUSPECT without LLM; stop on empty wave or depth limit with visited set. Engine is a pure iterator and never calls an LLM; sweep resumes events with no completed_at. One transaction per ripple is impossible once a wave waits on a user.

nodes.label: Wave (set of dependents resolved together)
nodes.rationale: Each wave is two commits; decisions tagged with wave number; wave 0 = deterministic restoration recorded by an answer.

nodes.label: Worked example: cgpa 7.6 -> 7.9 ripple

nodes.label: ADR-0013: Wave-by-wave ripple over core link classes
nodes.norm_label: adr-0013: wave-by-wave ripple over core link classes
nodes.rationale: Graph decides scope, LLM decides action; need chains of 3+ hops and a link class that never propagates. Engine emits waves along depends_on links; each wave commits as one transaction; keep halts a branch; ask parks memory in PENDING_USER and marks subtree SUSPECT; two link classes (depends_on, snapshot_of) in core; engine never calls an LLM (I3). Decided in kickoff interview; transaction boundary and two-class reduction from architecture-guardian review.
nodes.revisit_if: RippleBench chain scenarios show closure-first catches dependents the wave approach misses, or a domain needs behaviour neither class expresses
nodes.status: Accepted (approved by author same day); amends ADR-0003, ADR-0004, wording of ADR-0007/I7
nodes.tradeoffs: Rejected full transitive closure first (more LLM cost and over-correction), one transaction per ripple (impossible with LLM/user waits; hides SUSPECT from retrieval), per-link-type policy registry (testability), separate depends_on/derived_from classes, fixed generic types only (loses typed signal for link finder). Cost: latency grows with chain depth; wrong keep stops propagation; whole subtree SUSPECT while ask pending; crash leaves open ChangeEvent resumed by nightly sweep.

nodes.label: ADR-0014: Memory versions are rows; dependency links are copied to the new version
nodes.norm_label: adr-0014: memory versions are rows; dependency links are copied to the new version
nodes.rationale: Without copying, dependents' links point at the old row and the graph dies after one ripple. Every version is its own Memory row with supersedes_id; update in one transaction writes new row, retires old, copies incoming and outgoing depends_on links (outgoing re-pointed at parents' latest), leaves snapshot_of on the old row. History links (parent superseded) are skipped by inspector and retrieval expansion. From kickoff interview and architecture-guardian review.
nodes.revisit_if: Link-copy bugs appear in pilot or update latency exceeds NFR; then supersede with stable-identity design
nodes.tradeoffs: Rejected stable identity with history table (author prefers one table; copy rule gives snapshot semantics free), move/re-point (loses history), leaving outgoing links to Linker only (one missed link detaches version), overwrite in place. Cost: every update is a graph rewrite that must be transactional (NFR-4); link rows grow; in-memory and Postgres stores must share the filter.

nodes.norm_label: adr-0015: every change is a memory write; temporary facts self-expire

Trigger of every ripple is a memory write (new, new version incl. user edit, or expiry); temporary fact is an ordinary memory with valid_to; ChangeEvent gains trigger_kind; retrieval treats PENDING_USER like SUSPECT. Points 1-2 decided in kickoff; 3-4 are collaborator's recommended option, open to reversal.
nodes.revisit_if: Author answers question 5 differently (supersede points 3-4), or expiry ripples prove noisy because detector fills valid_to badly
nodes.tradeoffs: Rejected separate ChangeRequest entity, polymorphic ChangeEvent.trigger, classifying temporary only in detector without valid_to. Cost: FakeClock scenario for FR-5; one I2 invariant test per trigger kind; sweep needs index on valid_to.

nodes.label: ForgetEvent
nodes.rationale: Forget is deletion, not a state change, so it has no ChangeEvent (I7).

nodes.label: Invariant I7: forget deletes whole version chain and cascades
nodes.norm_label: invariant i7: forget deletes whole version chain and cascades
nodes.rationale: Forget applies to a whole version chain and cascades along depends_on links whose parent is in the chain; ADR-0007 calls this cascading along derived_from links.

nodes.label: Link type registry: depends_on_fact, depends_on_time_period, eligibility_of, fit_of, reminder_for, criteria_from, sent_with_resume
nodes.norm_label: link type registry: depends_on_fact, depends_on_time_period, eligibility_of, fit_of, reminder_for, criteria_from, sent_with_resume
nodes.rationale: sent_with_resume is snapshot_of so a new resume never ripples into past applications; all others are depends_on. Provenance to sources is source_ref, not a link, because sources are not memories.

nodes.label: Link class: depends_on
nodes.rationale: Propagates a change; copied to new version on update; on forget of parent the dependent is hard-deleted (cascade).

nodes.label: Link class: snapshot_of
nodes.rationale: Does not propagate; not copied to the new version; on forget of parent the link is removed and dependent kept. Makes the correct non-update case for sent applications fall out of the copy rule.

nodes.label: Link classes (core) vs link types (domains)
nodes.rationale: Core knows two classes with fixed behaviour; each domain link type maps to exactly one; the registry lives in the domain adapter and is applied in the write flow, never in core.

nodes.label: Versioning: copy incoming and outgoing depends_on links to the new version
nodes.norm_label: versioning: copy incoming and outgoing depends_on links to the new version
nodes.rationale: Incoming links copied so the new version has same dependents (retired dependents not copied; one per dependent,type); outgoing links copied re-pointed at each parent latest version so later parent changes still reach the new version even if the Linker misses; snapshot_of stays on old row; crash rolls back everything (ADR-0014).

nodes.label: ADR-0031 Jobs rule resolvers recompute derived beliefs from parents
nodes.norm_label: adr-0031 jobs rule resolvers recompute derived beliefs from parents
nodes.rationale: Derived beliefs (eligibility, fit, reminder, criteria) are arithmetic over structured fields so bench claim C4 needs them to never require a model call; content and structured value are pure functions of parents.
nodes.tradeoffs: A wrong rule is confidently wrong; content formats become a contract between derivation and rules; eligibility asymmetry (no cutoff = eligible, no CGPA = no belief).

nodes.label: ADR-0032 Ranking openings: eligible, urgent, fit, variety; flagged never retired
nodes.norm_label: adr-0032 ranking openings: eligible, urgent, fit, variety; flagged never retired
nodes.rationale: Ranking must come from memory-layer beliefs, not JD recomputation, otherwise stale beliefs are invisible to the layer that flags them (I1, C2). Tiers are explainable to students unlike a weighted score.
nodes.tradeoffs: Fit-before-urgency and weighted score rejected; past-deadline openings vanish from list but stay in memory; missing CGPA ranks cutoff openings as not eligible.

nodes.label: ADR-0042 Inspector endpoints: I1 at boundary, history on request, edits straight to versioning
nodes.norm_label: adr-0042 inspector endpoints: i1 at boundary, history on request, edits straight to versioning
nodes.rationale: FR-12 inspector; edit named by the user so Intake change detection would only guess and an LLM NEW verdict could duplicate prose memories; forget is the only deletion path (I7).
nodes.tradeoffs: Edits skip the Linker so new versions gain no new links; question text not stored so decision reason shown.

nodes.label: ADR-0045 Conversation agent: one LangGraph turn, strict intent, evidence-only answers
nodes.norm_label: adr-0045 conversation agent: one langgraph turn, strict intent, evidence-only answers
nodes.rationale: FR-10/FR-7 with I5 (no invention) and I6 (no external action); claim schema makes support structural; agent must reuse Intake and core.answers, not reimplement.
nodes.tradeoffs: True claims with forgotten citations are dropped; misread-but-cited claims not caught; numeric-only grounding; checkpoint is user text outside forget API; prompts jobs-flavoured.

nodes.label: ADR-0046 Tailor agent: read-only, picks from id-validated candidates
nodes.norm_label: adr-0046 tailor agent: read-only, picks from id-validated candidates
nodes.rationale: FR-11 suggest real projects without inventing; model good at matching, bad at being trusted with the project list; docs/02 gives Tailor read-only permission.
nodes.tradeoffs: Suggestions only as complete as candidate set; domain-specific by design; model-written paragraphs and persisted suggestions rejected.

nodes.label: ADR-0050 Lexical BM25/FTS, RRF fusion, one-hop graph expansion for retrieval
nodes.norm_label: adr-0050 lexical bm25/fts, rrf fusion, one-hop graph expansion for retrieval
nodes.rationale: Offline and Postgres backends must behave alike; I1 visibility enforced last in retriever, not in backends; follows ADR-0014 over the WS-5 brief (snapshot_of links followed).
nodes.tradeoffs: Postgres lexical path searches content only (parity gap); dense path only exercised by fake embedder; up to 2k rows returned; backends oversample 4k+16.

nodes.label: ADR-0055 Digest and alert policy: thresholds, rendering, what never alerts
nodes.norm_label: adr-0055 digest and alert policy: thresholds, rendering, what never alerts
nodes.rationale: FR-9 fixes no threshold or message shape; flagged items must not push users to act on doubted beliefs; plain text cannot fail Telegram rendering.
nodes.tradeoffs: Thresholds are policy not measurements; renderer does not catch invented numbers in fit_reasons; empty digest sends nothing.

nodes.label: ADR-0056 Worker jobs idempotent per user; per-user sweep lease; UTC schedule
nodes.norm_label: adr-0056 worker jobs idempotent per user; per-user sweep lease; utc schedule
nodes.rationale: arq cron may fire twice and retries happen; two sweeps resuming the same event would double-resolve the wave; digests must not duplicate.
nodes.tradeoffs: Lease stops sweep-vs-sweep but not sweep-vs-slow-live-ripple; InMemoryDeliveryLog forgets on restart; global lease and per-event runner lease deferred.

nodes.label: ADR-0060 Baseline memory strategies behind one MemoryStrategy protocol
nodes.norm_label: adr-0060 baseline memory strategies behind one memorystrategy protocol
nodes.rationale: Fair H1 comparison needs same writes, scripted resolver, clock and same cost counting; only propagation should vary.
nodes.tradeoffs: as_runner cast; Mem0-style baseline undecided; real-resolver over-correction is Phase 3.

nodes.label: ADR-0061 RippleBench v0 jobs track generated from seeded personas and templates
nodes.norm_label: adr-0061 ripplebench v0 jobs track generated from seeded personas and templates
nodes.rationale: Hand-written scenarios drift and item-level splits leak into link-finder training; split by persona and template; seeded RNG keeps persona i stable.
nodes.tradeoffs: Data small and regular so v0 measures engine not language; template change changes every persona file; LLM-generated scenarios deferred to v1.

nodes.label: ADR-0062 Time-to-consistency replay harness with per-event snapshots
nodes.norm_label: adr-0062 time-to-consistency replay harness with per-event snapshots
nodes.rationale: Rate metrics do not say how long a stale belief survives; snapshots after every event let TTC and stale-action window be computed, and gold checks read the same snapshot as the metrics.
nodes.tradeoffs: Stub action layer reads content heuristically; snapshots per alias only; larger results/ runs.

nodes.label: ADR-0063 Metric definitions for RippleBench v0
